recurringClusterFamilies.description: THE #1 GENERIC ENGINE DEFECT. The reconstruction ships no webfont and no @font-face rule anywhere: 0 occurrences of '@font-face' in the 11,267,135-byte public/wr/generated-styles.css, 0 in app/globals.css, and no .woff/.woff2/.ttf/.otf file anywhere under the prebuilt app. All 24 clone captures report document.fonts faceCount 0 / loadedFaces []; all 16 live-source captures report faceCount 3 with 'Inter Variable' (axis 100 900) and 'Berkeley Mono' loaded. Only the family STRING survives - 4,188 rules declare font-family:"Inter Variable","SF Pro Display",-apple-system,... and 109 declare the Berkeley Mono stack - so every glyph on every route is painted by the host fallback (measured as '.SF NS'/system-ui via CDP). It is made worse by variable-axis weights: 1,472 rules request font-weight:510 and 76 request 590, values no static fallback can hit, so they round UP to a bold face. Measured cost: +9% to +42% ink coverage on identical strings, 1.9-3.8% narrower advances, and re-wrapping on essentially every multi-line block on 7 of 8 routes. Root cause is structural, not a tuning gap: app/layout.tsx emits no <head>, and the pipeline never captured a font asset at all (asset-catalog.json kindCounts contains no font kind on any page), so nothing downstream could bind one. Named in src/reconstruction/types.ts as 'font-source-binding-unverified' and 'source-head-not-reconstructed' - but 'unverified' understates it: the binding is ABSENT, and this single family is present in all 19 audited pairs.

SVG paint is never observed and never reconstructed, so icons that the real page paints via CSS or via a CSS custom property render at the SVG initial value BLACK. Two mechanisms, one root: (a) 'fill' and 'stroke' are absent from STYLE_WHITELIST (src/observer/types.ts:260-434, verified 0 matches) and generated-styles.css emits 0 'fill:' and 0 'stroke:' declarations, so a <path> whose paint comes from a stylesheet rule falls back to black; (b) the pipeline preserves fill="var(--color-...)" presentation attributes verbatim into reconstruction-data (779 such attributes across the 8 pages: p1=77, p2=48, p3=2, p4=18, p5=76, p6=12, p7=504, p8=42) while generated-styles.css defines ZERO CSS custom properties, so every one of them is invalid-at-computed-value-time and reverts to black. Visible cost ranges from cosmetic to blocker depending on background: on /pricing the entire feature-comparison grid of ~200 check/cross marks and every plan-card bullet becomes invisible; on /security 21 of the page's icons vanish; on /integrations the CTA's white '+' disc inverts to black. Inline SVGs authored with fill="currentColor" render correctly (color IS whitelisted), which cleanly isolates the mechanism.

PSEUDO_STYLE_WHITELIST (src/observer/types.ts:484-521) is a closed 18-property list that omits opacity, visibility, mask-*, padding, border, margin and background-size/position, and its own comment states 'Nothing else was added. `opacity` and `visibility` would change how such a box LOOKS and no measurement has asked for them yet.' The consequence is systematic: a decorative pseudo that the real page holds at opacity:0 until hover is reproduced at full strength. Verified: 0 of the 2,258 pseudo rules in generated-styles.css carry any opacity declaration, and 1,128 of them paint a non-transparent background or background-image. Worst cases: /pricing emits 57 row-hover chips at rgb(20,21,22) per viewport, striping the whole comparison table (desktop, mobile AND wide) and accounting for ~89% of that route's changed pixels; /customers emits 61 rgba(255,255,255,0.05) row chips that merge into one phantom 1328x3418 panel (88.9% of that route's changed pixels). The same whitelist gap in a different direction turns /plan's three gradient-BORDER cards into filled rectangles (no mask/mask-composite/padding on pseudos) and strips the breadcrumb separator's side margins on /customers/automattic.

The generator bakes the observed computed pixel box onto essentially every element - 5,740 explicit width:<px> and 5,791 explicit height:<px> declarations (counted with a property-boundary regex). This is what makes document height match to 0-1px on 15 of 19 audited pairs while paint differs by 5-50%, and it converts every downstream text-metric difference into a NEW defect class instead of a harmless reflow: text that needs more room overflows and overprints its neighbours (r000001 mobile app-mock rows, r000002 desktop entries), text that needs less leaves dead space inside a pinned box (r000004 desktop/mobile, r000005 mobile, r000008 mobile), shrink-to-fit widths measured against Inter force wraps under the fallback (r000005 desktop/mobile bylines at width:49.625px and width:93.5625px), and a fixed-height parent kills last-child bottom-margin collapse so a whole section lands 80px off (r000008 desktop AND mobile). CRITICAL QA IMPLICATION: identical document height and 0.01px geometry medians are NOT evidence of layout fidelity here - they are a direct artifact of this baking.

assetMode 'reference' with assetDownloads 0 / remoteAssetUrls 404 does not merely leave the clone non-independent - on two routes it loses content outright. (b) A silent generator drop: src/reconstruction/asset-resolver.ts:25 declares PRIMARY_IMAGE_KINDS = ['image','source','video-poster'] with 'video' absent, so a

STYLE_WHITELIST is a closed allowlist and every modern text-shaping property the sites actually use falls outside it - verified 0 matches in src/observer/types.ts for text-wrap, -webkit-line-clamp / line-clamp, counter-increment, counter-reset, hanging-punctuation, font-variation-settings, font-feature-settings and -webkit-font-smoothing, and correspondingly 0 occurrences of each in generated-styles.css. Observed consequences: /plan (desktop and mobile) loses text-wrap:balance so every heading and caption re-rags greedily, including a break inside the hyphenated compound 'end-to-end'; /integrations (desktop and mobile) loses the -webkit-line-clamp ellipsis on 8 clamped card descriptions; the home page's code viewer prints '00' on every gutter line because 80 rules reference counter(line, decimal-leading-zero) with no counter-increment/reset anywhere; testimonial pull-quotes lose hanging punctuation. These are independent of the font family defect and would remain after fonts are fixed.

src/reconstruction/layout-inference.ts emits 'recovered' fluid rules at selector specificity (0,3,0) that OUTRANK the exact observed .wr-stXXXXXX class (0,1,0). Site-wide it emitted 1,910 such rules on desktop only - 1,148 width:auto and 52 width:<percent> (independently recounted in this synthesis; p000002 has 482 auto + 29 percent, p000003 281+13, p000007 129+3). Two audited routes show it producing visibly wrong geometry: on /changelog a percentage-width derived against a 1280px parent is applied to a node that is actually a 624px GRID ITEM (48.61% x 623.875 = 303.27px), halving the body column of all 10 entries and making the page's own content illegible - the single 'unusable' verdict in this audit; on /pricing a width:auto override replaces the observed width:1344px on the customer-logo <ul>, collapsing a space-between flex row to a 805px shrink-to-fit blob at desktop and wide. The module's stated guarantee at layout-inference.ts:19-22 ('every emitted rule must REPRODUCE the observed truth-viewport geometry, so the 1440px rendering cannot regress by construction') is empirically false; its only guard, TRUTH_SANITY_TOLERANCE_PX (layout-inference.ts:35), compares probe numbers and never lays the rule out.

Not a reconstruction defect: linear.app changed after the 2026-08-25 observation. Confirmed drift is confined to (a) the home page, wholly redesigned below the hero (live 9,960px vs accepted 10,898px at 1440; a new 'POWERING THE COMPANIES...' eyebrow with 0 hits in the August rendered.html), (b) /customers, whose table lost rows (live 4,886px vs accepted 7,134px), (c) /plan (live 14,771px vs accepted 10,665px), and (d) footer/nav link labels site-wide ('AI'/'Now' live vs 'Diffs'/'Monitor'/'Blog' in both the accepted source AND the clone). On the routes where both an ACCEPTED and a CURRENT_SOURCE comparison exist against the same clone, the two scores are within 0.1% of each other on /changelog (5,441,178 vs 5,441,210 changed px), /customers/automattic (491,293 vs 491,445), /integrations (374,420 vs 374,572) and /security (214,116 vs 214,251) - so drift explains none of the reported clusters.

Not a reconstruction defect: autoplay/loop hero videos, scroll-triggered reveals and a per-load letter-scramble cannot be frame-matched between two independent captures. Recorded so the adjudicator does not double-count them - on /plan desktop the hero video frame alone accounts for 14% of that pair's changed pixels (band-00 at cr 65%). Note the interaction with DEAD_ANIMATIONS: the clone is frozen forever rather than merely at a different phase, which turns a capture artifact into a permanent visual state on the scramble text.

The observer records open shadow hosts but not their rendered shadow content, so a custom element that paints its visible text inside a shadow root reconstructs as its light-DOM SSR fallback. On /pricing the <number-flow-react> price component loses the 'US' currency prefix and the two-tone amount/unit colour split ('US$10' + grey 'per user/month' becomes a uniform white '$10 per user/month') at desktop, mobile and wide. Verified not to be drift: the same element measures 170 css px of ink in BOTH the accepted August capture and today's live capture, versus 140 px in the clone. Named limitation 'shadow-content-not-observed' (src/reconstruction/types.ts, present in reconstruction-manifest.json).

At the 1920 'wide' profile - which is explicitly NOT an accepted viewport (metrics.json viewportProfile.accepted=false; the reconstruction carries only desktop 1440 and mobile 390 variants) - every fluid left/right anchoring that was flattened into observed pixels fails to stretch. On the home page the hero's full-bleed backdrop is frozen at width:1416px/left:12px/right:12px and renders as a letterboxed 1416px box with ~250px black bars, against the live div.WS84WW_background box of (12,527,1896x832) = the same authored rule evaluated at 1920. On /pricing the sticky table-header backdrop is frozen at left:672px/width:1440px and paints only the right half of the page. Documented here as a bounded, expected consequence of an unobserved profile, not as evidence about the accepted viewports.

generated-styles.css contains 0 @keyframes (verified) while declaring 26 non-none animation-name values (xt7VyG_scroll, xt7VyG_scroll-abs, w9ZFkq_staggerIn, _4phDSW_cursorIn, qM9FAa_cursorBlink, PPSGPG_blink, w9ZFkq_shine). Every CSS animation in the clone is therefore permanently dead, and each animated element renders frozen at whatever base/observed state it inherited. Visible as parked customer-logo marquees on r000001 mobile, r000007 mobile and r000008 desktop and as a static isometric illustration offset. This is separate from, and worse than, capture-frame variance: a frame race is unavoidable, a marquee that can never move is a missing capability.

STYLE_WHITELIST captures mask-image/size/position/repeat and the -webkit- aliases (src/observer/types.ts:362-369) but NOT mask-composite, mask-mode, mask-clip or mask-origin, and generated-styles.css contains 0 'mask-composite' and 0 'mask-mode' across 8,594 mask-image declarations. A multi-layer mask that only fades under mask-composite:intersect therefore composites with the default 'add' and is opaque nearly everywhere. On the home page the three source nodes carrying a 3-layer mask-image are EXACTLY the three worst bands (cr 61/36/46): product-mock panels that should dissolve into the background render fully opaque with visible panel borders and extra board columns. The same gap is what makes /plan's gradient-border rings paint as filled rectangles.

One accepted reference artifact is itself broken and no gate caught it. The p000002 mobile observation screenshot is a near-blank 73,446px column: only 807 rows (1.10%) contain any non-background pixel, and its 487,863-byte file size is the sole outlier among the 16 accepted screenshots (every other mobile screenshot is 1,287,126-4,957,611 bytes; p000002's own desktop is 4,046,539). The evidence PNG is byte-identical to the stored observation (md5 116a9b8299bd55ccbb0a095a6c028882). The same run's mobile styles.json records opacity:1 on 505/571 rules and visibility:visible on 533, i.e. the observer's own style probe saw a fully painted page. The clone is the MORE correct side of that comparison. Any QA gate reading that pair's 0.2221 screenshotChangedRatio as clone infidelity is measuring against a blank reference - and the QA run did exactly that.

The generator emits BOTH the desktop and the mobile variant subtree into one document and hides the inactive one with display:none via app/globals.css media queries. That is invisible for ordinary content but fatal for SVG paint servers: 347 SVG resource ids are duplicated between the two subtrees, and a live probe of the served clone found 46 of 46 url(#...) paint references inside [data-wr-viewport="mobile"] resolving to elements inside the display:none desktop subtree - a paint server with no layout object, which paints nothing. On /plan mobile this kills all 10 VfJKka_mask gradient fade overlays; every product mock and the hero lose their fade-out and render content the design deliberately hides, accounting for 78.1% of that pair's changed pixels over 37.8% of page height. Removing the hidden desktop subtree in-page restores the fades exactly. The same dual-subtree emission also inflates element counts (e.g. 6,569 clone DOM elements vs 4,453 observed on /changelog) and duplicates text lines in structure probes.

Eleven mix-blend-mode:overlay film-grain layers on the home page were captured with computed background-image 'none' and the texture bitmap was never captured as an asset at all (generated-styles.css has 0 occurrences of 'grain'; the live site fetches static.linear.app/.../grain-default.png). The panels therefore render mathematically flat (stdev 0.000 vs the source's 0.537-0.591) and 1-2 levels brighter. This is what produces bands where changedRatio approaches 1.0 at a meanDelta of only 5-17 - i.e. a defect that is nearly invisible per-pixel but covers enormous area, exactly the pattern that makes screenshotChangedRatio hard to interpret.

The clone's real <html>/<body> are unstyled Next.js framework elements (backgroundColor rgba(0,0,0,0), color rgb(0,0,0), fontFamily 'Times') and the page ground is painted by a re-emitted wrapper div instead. On these 8 routes the wrapper happens to cover the full document so nothing bleeds through, but it is a latent whole-page failure (white overscroll, or a white band wherever the wrapper does not cover the viewport). The pipeline's own QA already knows: reconstruction-qa final-summary.json carries classification 'canvas-background-mismatch' with 16 occurrences across 16 affected pages, upstreamStages {reconstruction:16}, not auto-fixed.

The clone freezes a post-load DOM state the source screenshot never reached: /changelog's <video preload=metadata> control bars render duration, scrub track and remaining-time labels in the clone (with the time labels breaking mid-number) where the source captured the pre-loadedmetadata state. Direction cannot be graded - there is no source counterpart - so it is reported, not scored.

A single measured offset with two inseparable causes; reported with both named rather than attributed. On /pricing wide, everything below the logo strip is 11-12px high, but part of the 14px strip-height difference is genuine source drift (the live strip is 40px tall; the August observation's was 28px).
One-off symptom whose mechanism could not be traced to code from the available artifacts; reported so it is not silently dropped.

metrics.json comparisonRules.changedPixel counts a pixel as changed when ANY channel differs by >= 1. On dark UI surfaces a 1-4/255 fill difference is invisible yet paints huge solid blocks in the diff: on r000001 mobile, 1,002 30x30 blocks are >85% changed with a mean delta below 40. Recorded so changedRatio is not read as a perceptual measure.
Per-load randomised source content (a letter-scramble animation) that no clone can match by construction.
Sub-perceptual difference (max channel delta 3) measured but not traced to a mechanism.

answer_isRawReconstructionVisuallyWrong: Yes - decisively, and generically rather than route-by-route. Across 19 independently audited source/clone pairs the raw exact reconstruction is 'obviously-different' on 17, 'unusable' on 1 (/changelog desktop) and 'minor-visible-differences' on exactly 1 (/customers/automattic at the unobserved 1920 profile); no pair is visually equivalent. The near-perfect geometry the QA run reported is real but misleading: document height matches to 0-1px on 15 of 19 pairs and element boxes agree sub-pixel wherever auditors measured them, yet 2.35% to 49.53% of pixels differ, because the generator bakes 5,740 explicit width:<px> and 5,791 explicit height:<px> declarations from the observation, so no paint or text-metric error can ever move a box - it overflows, overprints, or leaves a hole inside a frozen one instead. Every large-area defect traces to a small number of closed-allowlist and generator gaps that are verifiable in the current code and in the shipped artifact, not to hypotheses: the 11.2MB generated-styles.css contains 0 @font-face rules, 0 CSS custom-property declarations, 0 @keyframes, 0 'fill:'/'stroke:' declarations, 0 mask-composite, 0 text-wrap, 0 line-clamp and 0 counter-increment, while carrying 4,188 Inter-stack font-family rules, 1,472 font-weight:510 declarations, 779 surviving fill="var(--...)" attributes in reconstruction-data, 26 animation-name declarations, 8,594 mask-image declarations and 2,258 pseudo rules of which not one carries opacity. The result is that all 24 clone captures load ZERO font faces against the live site's 3; ~200 check marks on /pricing and 21 icons on /security paint black-on-black; 57 hover chips per viewport on /pricing and 61 on /customers paint permanently, striping 26-44% of those pages; and on /plan mobile all 10 gradient fade masks are inert because their url(#...) paint servers resolve into the display:none desktop variant subtree the generator ships in the same document. Two further defects are generator logic errors rather than observation gaps: layout-inference's recovered rules at specificity (0,3,0) override the exact observed width on 1,200 nodes site-wide and halve the /changelog body column (48.61% of a 624px grid area = 303px), and asset-resolver's PRIMARY_IMAGE_KINDS omits 'video', silently dropping four <video> sources on /customers while the manifest still reports unresolvedElementAssets: 0. Source drift is real on 4 routes but explains none of it - on the four routes where the same clone was scored against both the August observation and a live capture taken on the audit date, the two scores differ by under 0.1%. One caveat cuts the other way and must be carried forward: the accepted p000002 mobile reference screenshot is itself blank (1.10% of rows painted, 487KB against 1.3-5.0MB for every other mobile capture), so that pair's 0.2221 ratio measures a broken reference, not a broken clone.
limitations: Static full-page screenshots only. Scroll-driven sticky/fixed behaviour, hover, focus, menu-open and other interactive after-states were NOT exercised on any pair; where a header is position:fixed the audit can only say it paints identically at scroll 0.

Animated surfaces cannot be frame-matched. Autoplay/loop hero videos (r000006), scroll-reveal demos (r000006), marquees (r000001/r000007/r000008) and the per-load letter-scramble (r000008) contribute changed pixels that are not attributable to reconstruction fidelity; on r000006 desktop the hero video alone is ~14% of that pair's changed pixels.

The 1920 'wide' profile has no accepted source of truth (metrics.json viewportProfile.accepted=false) and was compared only against live captures taken on the audit date, so its 3 pairs mix clone defects with source drift by construction. Only 3 of 8 routes were captured at wide.

changedRatio counts any channel delta >= 1, so it is not a perceptual metric: r000001 mobile has 1,002 30x30 blocks that are >85% 'changed' at a mean delta below 40, and several bands reach cr 1.00 at meanDelta 5-17 from an invisible flat-vs-grain difference.

The clone captures ran WITH live network access to Linear's CDN, so 15 of 24 captures show zero asset failures. This audit therefore measures the clone as a hotlinking page, not as the independent artifact the product requires; the historical QA run's 202 assetFailures is what the same clone looks like when the CDN is unreachable and was NOT reproduced here.

-webkit-font-smoothing could not be separated from face substitution as a contributor to the measured +9-42% ink coverage; the property is absent from STYLE_WHITELIST and the original stylesheets are not compiled, so neither the presence nor the absence of an authored 'antialiased' can be proven from the stored evidence.
Two clusters remain untraced to code: the r000001 changelog timeline dots (VC-07) and the r000004 wide header right-end 1-3/255 background lift (VC-111). Both are reported with measurements only.

The r000002 mobile pair cannot grade mobile paint fidelity at all, because its accepted reference screenshot is blank; and r000002's 'unusable' desktop verdict rests on a defect (percentage-width on a grid item) that this audit measured on one route - the emitter's 1,148 width:auto and 52 width:% overrides site-wide were counted but their individual correctness was not re-laid-out.
